source_name: ЕНЕР — draft-regulation detail pages for FX / financial-sector laws (worked examples)
why_relevant: Concrete evidence that financial-sector drafts really are consulted on ENER: a draft Law amending the Law on Foreign Exchange Operations (Закон за девизното работење), explicitly framed as harmonisation with the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems. Shows the exact document set (draft text + RIA report + consultation window) our collector should expect.

source_name: Огледало на Владата — ENER monitoring (monthly / quarterly consultation-compliance reports)
why_relevant: Civil-society watchdog that systematically monitors what ministries put on ENER, whether consultation windows were respected, and which drafts bypassed consultation. Excellent quality-control layer and a second index over the same consultation universe — catches drafts that were pushed through by shortened procedure and would otherwise be missed.

source_name: Собрание на РСМ — Законодавна постапка and session materials (parliamentary pipeline)
why_relevant: Downstream leg of the deadline chain: once a consulted draft becomes a Government bill it appears here with first/second reading dates, amendments and committee materials. Procedural rules are published (materials circulated 15 days before a session for laws; second reading within 7 working days of the first-reading plenary), which lets us convert a bill's appearance into a dated forecast of entry into force.

source_name: Службен весник на РСМ (Official Gazette)
why_relevant: Legal system of record. Every NBRM decision and every law carries an Off. Gazette number and date; the gazette issue date starts the vacatio legis and any transition deadline. Indispensable for closing the loop from consulted draft -> binding obligation with a hard compliance date.

source_name: Македонска банкарска асоцијација (МБА) — Macedonian Banking Association
why_relevant: The de facto consultee. Because NBRM has no open comment portal, its consultation is largely channelled through the banking association and working groups with member banks; MBA's news/tag streams surface joint NBRM-MoF-MBA work on draft regulation (e.g. the rules on changing contractual conditions for credit exposures) and NBRM guidance for banks before or around publication. Best proxy for 'a draft exists and industry is commenting on it'.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Закони и прописи / draft laws
why_relevant: Formal proposer of financial-sector primary legislation (banking, payments, FX, financial discipline). Publishes draft bills and occasionally opens 'јавна расправа' outside ENER, plus the Правни работи section that tracks its legislative pipeline. Upstream of every NBRM bylaw wave.

source_name: НПАА — Национална програма за усвојување на правото на ЕУ (Chapter 4 free movement of capital / Chapter 9 financial services)
why_relevant: The most explicit multi-year regulatory calendar in the country: NPAA annexes give, per acquis chapter, the national acts to be adopted, the responsible institution (NBRM for Ch.4/Ch.9 items) and the target quarter/year. Converts EU-alignment obligations (PSD2-equivalent, CRD/CRR, resolution) into dated national deadlines long before any draft is circulated.

source_name: НБРСМ — English site: Supervision and About sections
why_relevant: English mirror of the supervisory pages; confirms the Banking Regulations Department owns the 'establishment and improvement of the banking supervision regulatory framework'. Useful for entity/actor mapping and for machine-readable English titles of decisions, though the English tree lags the Macedonian one and does not carry all draft/announcement content.

source_name: НБРСМ — Совет на Народната банка (Council composition and session outputs)
why_relevant: The Council is the adopting body: draft decisions become binding at a Council session, and the post-session release is the earliest public confirmation (e.g. the session adopting 12 decisions completing the bank-resolution framework; the 5 Dec 2025 session adopting the 2026 Work Programme). Actor-mapping this body lets us attribute and date every regulatory act.

source_name: MIA / Makfax / mba.mk — Macedonian financial press reporting on NBRM Council sessions
why_relevant: Because nbrm.mk is bot-defended, national wire and business media are a reliable, freely-crawlable mirror of NBRM regulatory announcements — they reproduce the Council-session releases verbatim (e.g. 'Донесена е регулатива за операционализација на Законот за решавање банки'). Serves as a redundancy channel and as an early tip-off for what to go fetch from nbrm.mk with a browser.

source_name: uslugi.gov.mk — National Bank institutional service catalogue
why_relevant: State service catalogue listing NBRM's administrative procedures (licences, consents, registrations) with their legal bases. Useful as a pointer that maps which bylaw governs which supervised-entity obligation, and it surfaces procedure changes that follow a new decision — a cheap, unblocked proxy for the bot-defended nbrm.mk.

source_name: НБРСМ official social channels (Facebook, X/@narodna_banka)
why_relevant: Lowest-latency public broadcast of NBRM announcements and, in practice, an unblocked mirror of soopstenija items with the canonical nbrm.mk link attached. Good tripwire for 'something regulatory was just published' when the website crawler is being 403'd.

source_name: Lexology (LexisNexis) — North Macedonia banking & finance law firm alerts
why_relevant: Aggregates client alerts from regional firms (Karanovic & Partners, BDK, CMS, ODI) covering MK payment services and capital markets laws, with English summaries and explicit application dates (e.g. Financial Instruments / Prospectus laws deferred to 1 October 2026).

source_name: Karanovic & Partners — news / legal updates (North Macedonia desk)
why_relevant: Regional SEE firm with a cooperating Skopje office; publishes English notes on MK payment services legislation and comparative PSD2 harmonisation across the region — useful for effective dates and practical compliance framing.

source_name: BDK Advokati — regional legal updates covering North Macedonia
why_relevant: Publishes detailed English explainers of MK financial-market legislation (Financial Instruments Law, Prospectus & Transparency Law) including revised application dates — a competitively fast secondary source.

source_name: CMS Law — North Macedonia banking & finance / capital markets practice pages
source_subtype: law firm country page / expert guide
why_relevant: Global firm with a MK country page; CMS publishes Expert Guides and law-now alerts that summarise local banking/payments regimes in English with comparative framing.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters — North Macedonia banking & finance coverage
why_relevant: Regional legal trade publication running annual 'Banking and Finance in North Macedonia' market overviews, non-banking financial sector explainers and SEPA-accession commentary; also a pointer to which local firms are active on which reforms.

source_name: Mondaq — North Macedonia FinTech Comparative Guide
why_relevant: Structured Q&A comparative guide on MK fintech/payments regulation (NBRNM authorisation of third-party payment providers, cybersecurity powers) — good baseline reference for regulatory perimeter questions.

source_name: IMF — Republic of North Macedonia country page (Article IV, staff reports, FSSA)
why_relevant: Authoritative English assessments of MK banking supervision, financial stability and reform commitments, with dated recommendations and structural-benchmark deadlines; archives content permanently.

source_name: IMF Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP / FSSA) publication index
why_relevant: Central index for FSAP/FSSA outputs including Basel Core Principles compliance assessments and technical notes; the canonical place to detect whether/when a new MK FSAP is scheduled or published.

source_name: World Bank — North Macedonia country hub and Documents & Reports
why_relevant: Publishes MK Policy Notes, payment-system modernisation work with the National Bank, and electronic-payments-acceptance diagnostics; documents repository archives PDFs that disappear from national sites.

source_name: World Bank corporate procurement — Western Balkans / North Macedonia payments RFx notices
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly: procurement notices for advisory work (electronic payments in MK, digital financial services legal diagnostics in the Western Balkans) disclose upcoming reform workstreams months before reports appear.

source_name: EBRD — North Macedonia country page, strategy and results snapshots
why_relevant: Country strategies and diagnostics set out financial-sector reform priorities and policy-dialogue commitments; EBRD legal transition work covers secured transactions and capital-market rules relevant to banking regulation.

source_name: European Commission — Enlargement package, North Macedonia annual country report
why_relevant: The single most systematic English scorecard of MK alignment on financial services (e.g. 2025 report: 'moderately prepared', progress on BRRD-aligned legislation); dated annually and archived on EUR-Lex as SWD documents.

source_name: Council of Europe MONEYVAL — North Macedonia evaluation and follow-up reports
why_relevant: AML/CFT mutual evaluation and follow-up reports rate MK against FATF recommendations including R.26 on financial-sector regulation and supervision; drives concrete supervisory reform deadlines for banks and PSPs.
